mechanism: Five original hole outlines form a concrete one-to-four punch-to-hole correspondence. It favors C by mistaking the left vertical fold boundary for an outer edge; it does not color a choice box, letter, or unrelated outline.
mathematical_solution: Normalize the original rectangle to [0,4] x [0,2]. Bottom-to-top maps y to 2-y on the moving half, leaving the stack in y in [1,2]. Left-to-right maps x to 4-x on the moving half, leaving x in [2,4]. The final punch lies near (2.25,1.75), as its frozen local coordinates (12.25,5.45) are 0.25 from the folded left side and 0.25 from its top. Reverse the folds: (2.25,1.75), (1.75,1.75), (2.25,0.25), (1.75,0.25). In B these are translated by +6 along x, giving its four exact centers (7.75/8.25,0.25/1.75). C instead has x=0.25/3.75 relative to its box, wrongly near outside edges; D is near both axes; E is near outside x and central y; A is not symmetric about both axes. Only B is the complete correct reflected orbit.
human_semantics: Only the pre-existing circle outlines are recolored. The punch X remains visible; every circle center, radius, white interior, original fold arrow, dashed fold line and option label is unchanged. These are proposed visual correspondences, not new holes, cuts, or a condition that physical red ink must survive a fold. No whole option is boxed. Native-size small circles require an explicit visual check.

marker_roles.role: Actual punch circle at X in the twice-folded sheet; source of the four reflected hole copies.
